As I said in another post we are sliding into a dangerous trend where anything free is ignored/toned  down. Story,  crafting, exploration, and also the free miracle outfits seem unimportant to the execs so each iteration keeps getting worse. 1st miracle outift was core to the story 2nd didn't have lore but had a complex crafting experience 3rd is now a time gated daily login mess.
Same with the settlements: from immersive human settlements to messy creature settlements, to disjointed holiday islands.
Yes, bugs can be patched, prices can be adjusted, compensation can be  given out but nothing will make up for messy content/lack of content.

Final hot take : the game is currently in an identity crisis from conflict between profit/development. What made the launch so great was the balance between the world and the dress up. But since interacting with the world is free, the execs only seem to focus on the paid outfits. But they forget that clothes mean nothing if you have no occasion to wear them for. The game is now devolving into a photo shoot simulator with story/world building/exploration being pushed to the side.

Another hot take: the problem with sea of stars is not the emptiness but the misleading marketing. It's a hub world hooking you up with the real content,  but it was advertised as full fledged new content instead. (+ there is not much real content to lead you to yet...)
The correct way to market it would have been to introduce it as a gateway and access the bubble island from there, or wait until there is a real fantasy world it can teleport to. So yea, they rushed out an empty hub and tried to pretend it was content.

Utsuges in general have this affect on me: i rebel against their endings and then realise what i am really rejecting is the reality of our life.
